DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The history of a rear-end collision (dashboard injury), the characteristic "pop," and the presentation of the leg in a shortened, internally rotated, and adducted position are classic signs of a posterior hip dislocation. The imaging results should confirm the femoral head is displaced posteriorly out of the acetabulum, and the MRI will likely show an associated posterior acetabular rim fracture and possible sciatic nerve injury. Immediate reduction is required to prevent further soft tissue damage and avascular necrosis.
